title: Deduplicate escalation filtering via shared summarizeEscalations() helper
context: Four independent code paths (CLI escalations, SessionStart, hunch_now MCP tool, hunch_escalations MCP tool) and the VS Code panel were each hand-rolling the logic to separate actionable from non-actionable escalations. This duplication allowed the VS Code panel to miss the actionable field entirely, causing it to miscount entries needing decisions. Touches invariant(s): con_7217ab24ab (Regression guard: "Flaky test failure under parallelism: native tree-sitter module resolution race on Windows" must not recur.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Extract escalation filtering into a single summarizeEscalations(items) → {actionable, context} helper function that all consumers call. Add the missing actionable field to VS Code's EscalationEntry interface. Tighten test assertions to validate through actionableEscalations() directly instead of loose per-field equality checks.
consequences: Eliminates the bug where VS Code's tally counted non-actionable entries
Makes the actionable/context distinction explicit in one place, not repeated across four callers
Forces any future consumer through the same filter — can't accidentally omit it
Test suite now covers all four consumer paths (CLI text, SessionStart, MCP tools), not just --json
Non-actionable entries remain visible for transparency, just not gated-on by the tally
alternatives_rejected: Patching only the VS Code panel would mask the underlying duplication and risk the same mistake in a fifth consumer
Using a shared constant or object property instead of a function would require all callers to compute context separately, leaving room for drift
